cells.tense: You are holding a start open and have not named where it goes.
cells.act: carry on with the version you chose through another week of doubt
cells.ask: Stay with a beginning you already made, same version, through another week of not knowing how it lands. No new decision, no explaining it to anyone. When doubt gets loud, finish the week anyway.
cells.core:
You can light something up before you know what it is. One step of ground is enough to move on, and the next one shows up. Uncertainty doesn't stall you the way it stalls most people — you go on the light you have, and it has been enough so far. That is what this balance is holding.

What it gets to feed next is staying with the same version another week, including the days it stops making sense. No new decision, and nobody needs to be told. A thing you chose once keeps showing what it is when you let it run past the moment you'd want to close it.

cells.tense: You are assembling the ending of a thing that has barely started.
cells.act: look at the whole of it until nothing is left to see
cells.ask: Lay out everything known and everything guessed about a beginning on one sheet, all of it visible at once. Study the whole sheet ten minutes and add nothing to it.
cells.core:
When something starts, you want the finish on the page first. Before the first move, there's a whole constructed picture — steps, outcomes, gaps filled in as though they were known. It passes for being thorough. What it's doing here is standing you ahead of your own life, busy with a shape that hasn't come, so the light you actually have goes unused.

The other side is being open, available, nothing already settled, every moment fresh because nothing has been decided for it. Lay out everything known and everything guessed about a beginning on one sheet, all of it visible at once. Study the whole of it ten minutes and add nothing. Seeing all of it is not the same as closing it.

cells.tense: You are near a beginning without entering it, and the nearness has become the place you live.
cells.act: take in the whole rainbow of what you feel
cells.ask: Note every feeling one ongoing thing brings you on a single page — all of them, none crossed out. Read it back the next day without sorting anything or acting on any of it.
cells.core:
Something wants to start through you and isn't starting. You stand close to the beginning without stepping in; the next step is lit and you aren't taking it. The readiness is here and the arrival isn't, and the not-arriving has gone on past the point where it could be called a moment.

Let feeling carry it instead of a plan. Every feeling one ongoing thing brings you goes on a single page, all of them, none crossed out, and the next day you read it back without sorting or choosing one to act on. You don't have to pick a feeling or move on any of it — just take the whole of what's there at once, complete, exactly as it is. A beginning can reach you through feeling before it reaches you through a decision.

cells.tense: You are deciding how to move through a blurry stretch and filing the decisions under circumstance.
cells.act: let the satisfaction of a finished thing land
cells.ask: Spend one evening with something you saw through to the end exactly as it stands — no next version, no fixing, no notes for later. Let what's done be done.
cells.core:
You can move through a fog with no clearing in it. Only the next step is visible, and that's the one you take, then the one after it — and you've been getting through on that, which is real. By your account, though, it just happens to you. Not a choice, not a skill. The way you handle uncertainty has been filed under the way things are.

Get back to what's already arrived. Something you saw through to the end — the parts that worked and the parts that didn't — sits with you one evening exactly as it stands. No next version, no fixing, no notes for later. Let the satisfaction of the finished thing land where it actually belongs, which is with the person who got it finished.
